Image.keepMounted.semantic: default behaviour preloads src and renders the only after it loads; true renders immediately and loads in place, enabling loading='lazy' and optimized image components such as next/image

Image.render.semantic: used to delegate to next/image etc.

Fallback.delay.semantic: ms to wait before showing the fallback (avoids flashing initials before the image resolves)

dataAttributes: Image: data-loading (while loading), data-error (failed to load), data-starting-style, data-ending-style
renderProp: Per-part `render` (ReactElement | (props, state) => ReactElement) via useRender — Image.render is the documented way to plug in next/image. Image's render-function props type is ImgHTMLAttributes<HTMLImageElement> rather than the generic HTMLProps.
controlled: Uncontrolled only — the component owns image loading status. The closest thing to control is Image.onLoadingStatusChange(status) plus the derived data-loading/data-error attributes. There is no open/close or value model.
formIntegration: None — no hidden inputs, name/value or validation. The rendered is decorative/identity only; pass alt text yourself.
keyboard: None — Avatar is non-interactive; it renders a , an and a fallback , with no focus management or key handling.
notableDifferences: No isDisabled/isLoading props: loading state is surfaced through data-loading / data-error attributes and the onLoadingStatusChange callback.

Default behaviour deliberately does NOT render the until the source has loaded (preload-then-mount), which is incompatible with loading='lazy' and with image optimizers that rewrite the URL unless you pass keepMounted.

With keepMounted you get SSR-visible markup and are expected to stack Image after Fallback in the DOM, hiding states via visibility (NOT display:none, which would break lazy loading) — a very different contract from a simple with an onError fallback.
Fallback.delay (ms) exists so initials do not flash while the image loads; React Aria has no such primitive.
No Avatar.Group / badge parts — only Root, Image, Fallback.
Root is a <span>, not a <div>, which matters when porting layout CSS.
